questions.q: Data is modeled in a Data 360 semantic model, and the audience will use dashboards on Salesforce record pages. Which tool is the natural default?
options: Tableau Desktop with a data extract
Tableau Next
A spreadsheet export
Neither can use a semantic model
questions.explain: Tableau Next is built into the Salesforce platform, works from the semantic model, and dashboards can be embedded in Lightning pages.

questions.q: Which situation most clearly favors Tableau Desktop?
options: The audience only uses Slack
You want sharing and governance handled inside Salesforce
One workbook must combine many non-Salesforce sources and needs deep authoring features
The data already lives in a semantic model
questions.explain: Desktop's mature authoring and broad connectivity fit multi-source, deeply customized work, and teams already fluent in it can stay productive.

questions.q: How can Tableau Desktop use the same definitions that Tableau Next uses?
options: By re-typing each calculation by hand
By exporting the semantic model to CSV
By connecting through the Tableau Semantics connector and selecting a semantic model
It cannot; the tools never share definitions
questions.explain: The Tableau Semantics connector lets Desktop and Tableau Cloud build on semantic models from Tableau Next and Data 360.

questions.q: Which is a limitation to expect when Tableau Desktop connects to a semantic model, per current Tableau documentation?
options: Extracts are not available, and some authoring features are limited
You can no longer create any charts
Every field must be re-authenticated each query
Only Salesforce administrators can connect
questions.explain: Because the connection relies on the source model, extracts are unavailable and features like sets, blending, and context filters are limited. Always check the current help page.

questions.q: Which is the best summary decision rule from this lesson?
options: Always choose Tableau Desktop because it is older
Always choose Tableau Next because it is newer
Pick by coin flip and migrate later
Match the tool to where the data lives, who consumes the result, and needed authoring depth, and model once in the semantic layer when both apply
questions.explain: Neither tool is universally better. Choose by data location, audience, authoring needs, and team skills, and reuse one semantic model when both are needed.
